newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish markets take government split in stride.
newsitem.headline: Danish markets take government split in stride.

text.p: Danish markets reacted calmly on Friday to the announcement that the small Centre Democrat party was to quit the ruling Social Democrat-led coalition, with bonds and shares only falling marginally.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 slipped 0.13 point to 109.16 shortly after the announcement.
The benchmark 2006 bond closed at 109.00 on Thursday close, opening on Friday at 109.50.
The fall caused the 10-year bond yield gap with Germany to widen four basis points to 82, while the crown currency fell a minimal 0.18 to 3.8278 to the mark on the news.
The top-20 KFX index stood at 132.22 at 1325 gmt, around 25 basis points down since the announcement but still 1.25 point above its opening level.

In a separate media statement, Danish Social Democrat Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said that his coalition would continue with its sole remaining partner, the Radical Liberals and that he would announce a cabinet reshuffle in January. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
